title: Contraction under signed product noise
statement: For every real $q>1$, there is a constant $c$ with $0<c\\le1$ such that $c=2/5$ whenever $q=4$ or $q=4/3$. For every natural number $n$, every product of $n$ finite probability spaces whose coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to one, every sign vector $s\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$, and every real-valued function $f$ on the product outcome space, the $q$-moment norm of the anisotropic noise transform with coordinate rates $cs_i$ is at most the $q$-moment norm of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: For every $q>1$ there exists $0<c\le1$, with $c=2/5$ when $q\in\{4,4/3\}$, such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every sign vector $s\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and every real $f$ on its outcome space, $\|T_{c\boldsymbol s}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$.
